slides.heading: Type Conversion
slides.body: Type Conversion is part of Mathematical and String Operations. This short lesson gives you a practical Python idea you can understand, try, and reuse in simple programs.

slides.heading: Core Idea: Type Conversion
slides.body: Type conversion changes a value from one data type to another. For example, int("25") changes text into a number.

slides.heading: Real-World Analogy
slides.body: Type conversion is like converting pesos to centavos. The value is related, but the form changes.

slides.heading: Try It Yourself!
slides.prompt: Convert the string "10" into an integer, add 2, and print the result.

quiz.prompt_text: What does int("25") do in Python?

options: Stores the string "25" without any change
Converts the text "25" into the integer 25
Converts the number 25 into the string "25"

quiz.explanation: Correct! int() converts a value to an integer. int("25") changes the text "25" into the number 25 so you can use it in calculations.

quiz.prompt_text: Arrange the following lines in the correct order to convert a string to an integer and add 5 to it.
quiz.explanation: The string is defined first, then int() converts it to an integer stored in number, and finally the addition is calculated and printed as 30.

quiz.prompt_text: Convert the string "10" into an integer, add 2 to it, and print the result.

content.hint: Use int(text) before adding. Then print the result.

quiz.correct_answer: Any valid Python code that satisfies the prompt.
quiz.explanation: number = int(text) converts the string to integer, then print(number + 2) outputs 12. Type conversion is needed before doing math on text input.
